record.summary: Vivek Anand signed a purchase agreement for a flat, paid a Rs 5,00,000 token, and three months later lost his job. He now wants to cancel the agreement, obtain a full refund of the token, and threaten legal action against the builder, claiming the cancellation clause is unfair. The builder has not defaulted and has offered to resell the flat or defer payments.
record.goal: Cancel the agreement, recover the full token amount, and assess the possibility of suing the builder for the alleged unfair clause.
questions: What is the exact date on which the purchase agreement was signed and the token amount was paid?
On which exact date did Vivek receive the termination letter and lose his job?
Did Vivek send any written notice of cancellation to the builder, and if so, on what date?
Has the builder responded in writing to Vivek's cancellation request beyond the offer to resell or defer?
Are there any other clauses in the agreement (e.g., force majeure, hardship) that might affect cancellation rights?
contradictions: Vivek seeks a full refund of the token, but clause 9 of the agreement expressly states that the token is forfeited if the buyer cancels for any reason other than the builder's default.
evidence: Signed agreement (22 pages, includes clause 9 on cancellation and forfeiture, initialed by Vivek on each page)
Payment receipt showing the Rs 5,00,000 token paid by bank transfer
Brochure and builder's emails showing consistent project descriptions
Progress report indicating construction is on schedule (building at fourth floor)
Termination letter from Vivek's employer confirming job loss
Builder's email offering resale assistance or deferment of payment
